audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Incorrect heavy-path boundary-layer width in Lemma6.8; All-positive-tilt uniformity in FS maximum bound fails
limitations: Incorrect heavy-path boundary-layer width in Lemma6.8 — Counterevidence: The proof gives an O(lambda^-k/2) boundary width; enlarging its constant could repair the geometry. A fixed lambda-dependent enlargement keeps total widthO_lambda(T^-15)<<T^-10.

Incorrect heavy-path boundary-layer width in Lemma6.8 — Counterevidence: Enlarging the boundary width by C_lambda>sqrt(2lambda) repairs the geometric margin and keeps the total width O_lambda(T^-15); the corrected probability estimate and induction are not certified.

All-positive-tilt uniformity in FS maximum bound fails — Counterevidence: The inspected core applications use large T and a>=1, so scaled time is bounded below. a>=1 alone does not justify absorption on arbitrarily short intervals.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:pbr. The one-line measure \(\mathcal L^{a;x,y}_{\ell,r}\) is the Brownian bridge from \(x>0\) to \(y>0\) on \([\ell,r]\), weighted by \(\exp(-a\int_\ell^r X(s)\,ds)\) and conditioned to remain positive (Definition 1.1, PDF p. 4). Thus, for strength \(2a\), the parabolic barrier representation is \[
 X(t)=Y(t)+at^2,\qquad
 Y\ \text{a standard Brownian bridge above }-at^2.\] This normalization follows directly from Lemma 2.4, PDF p. 13; using strength \(a\) instead would give the parabola \(at^2/2\). The Brownian variance convention is the one in the paper.

In the infinite ensemble, \(\lambda>1\) is fixed, the area strengths are \(2\lambda^{i-1}\), the curves are strictly ordered and positive, and the Brownian–Gibbs property resamples only finitely many curves on a bounded interval. Definition 1.7 additionally requires asymptotic pinning to zero. This assumption cannot be dropped: an upward translation preserves the Gibbs specification but changes the floor selected at infinity (PDF p. 8).

Theorems 1.3 and 1.8 classify extremal states by \((L,R)\in[-\infty,\infty)^2\) with \(L+R<0\); finite slopes, one slope equal to \(-\infty\), and both slopes equal to \(-\infty\) are distinct cases. Positive infinity is excluded. The parabolic coefficient is fixed by the tilt normalization. Time translation changes the slopes by \((L,R)\mapsto(L+2h,R-2h)\) at strength 2. Theorem 1.9 concerns lower lines and includes the time-scale term \(\lambda^{2k/3}\) inside the interval-maximum expectation. None of the counterexamples below violates these distinctions.
